hold_text: TIER-3, ORDER PATH. This PR changes src/units/accounts/ib_client.py's close-confirmation gate and MUST NOT MERGE without explicit operator approval. It is opened for review, deliberately: MI-167 wrote the fix in prose only, and MI-168 was dispatched to turn it into something specific enough to approve or reject. WHAT IT CHANGES: IBClient.close confirmed a close by requiring the whole SYMBOL to reach flat while the close is of a single TRADE, so whenever the account legitimately held other lots of that symbol the gate could never be satisfied however perfectly the close executed - and the failure branch deliberately leaves the journal row open. Measured on ib_paper/MGC 2026-09-07: order 547 sold all 43 of trade 5531's lots (Filled 43.0 @ 4392.9) and the close was graded a failure because sibling trade 5353 held 11 lots; a realised -$17,024.28 is absent from the book and 43 phantom stop lots were re-armed over an 11-lot position. The gate now confirms against the close order's OWN fill first, then a position reduction, then flatness. TWO DECISIONS ARE OWED, NOT ONE. (1) The re-scoping itself. (2) THE PARTIAL-REDUCTION QUESTION, which MI-167 left open and which this PR does NOT decide silently: IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_PARTIAL ships at `strict` (a 40-of-43 fill does NOT confirm, erring toward a phantom OPEN row) with `reduction` implemented and tested (erring toward a FABRICATED PnL on the unclosed remainder plus naked lots). Both behaviours and their consequences are in docs/design/close-confirmation-scope-DESIGN.md section 3. COUPLED TO MI-140 IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: MI-140 must not be remediated before this lands - alpaca_live is REAL MONEY and immune today only because it cannot place orders at all. Edges are written on both work objects. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not touch the venue, cancel a leg, or edit a journal row (the MGC remediation is separately operator-approved and is not this unit's); it adds NO confirmation to Bybit (bybit_2 is REAL MONEY, has no close-confirmation at all, and adding one would arm a new gate on real money - explicitly out of scope); and it does NOT apply MI-167's proposed identical change to alpaca_client.py, because MI-168 established by measurement that doing so would install a false-SUCCESS on a real-money-capable path (see section 6 of the memo). No Alpaca client code is touched.
why: Tier-3 by path and by content: it modifies the live order path (src/units/accounts/ib_client.py), which docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md places at Tier-3 - analyze and propose the exact change, merge only with explicit operator approval. The rest of the diff is Tier-1 (one design memo under docs/design/ and its DOCUMENT-INDEX row, one regression test under tests/, two work-object files recording the MI-140 coupling edge in both directions, and this landing declaration), but the PR takes the tier of its highest-tier file. landing=hold rather than self because the dispatch was explicitly PROPOSE-ONLY and because a human should read the partial-reduction risk decision before it binds. No config/, no risk caps, no strategy params, no account-mode flip, no workflow, no live-VM file, no journal write.
